summary: A panel of dual-enrollment specialists (Dr. Justin Osborn/ACCP, Steven Fu/Ohio State, Michelle Prince-Spetz/Syracuse, Vicki Shillington/counselor), moderated by Niharika Sondhi, explained how US high schoolers can earn transferable college credit while still in high school. The panel noted that roughly 80% of US high school students now have some form of dual-enrollment access, that universities typically cap transferable credit around 30 credits (about a year), and that students who earn credits while still enrolled in high school matriculate as freshmen, not transfer students, at their destination university.
keyInsights: ~80% of US high school students now have access to some form of dual enrollment.
Universities typically cap transferable dual-enrollment credit at around 30 credits (roughly one academic year).
Students who earn dual-enrollment credit while still in high school matriculate as freshmen, not as transfer students.
